message.content: The sea’s hue isn’t fixed—it shifts with depth, clarity, angle of light, and what’s floating in it. In clear, shallow waters you’ll often see bright turquoise or aquamarine because water absorbs longer wavelengths (red) and scatters shorter ones (blue). In deeper or murkier seas, the color can lean toward deep blue or even dark indigo. When algae bloom or sediment is stirred up, the water may look greenish‑yellow or brownish. So while “blue” is the classic image, the actual shade depends on a mix of physical and biological conditions.
